text:
Connor McDavid scored with 88 seconds left in the third period, deflecting a shot past Brandon Bussi on what the model rated a 2% chance, and the Oilers carried that goal into a shootout win over the Hurricanes, 6-5. Edmonton had trailed by two goals in the second period, and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins ended it in the third round of the shootout, the only shooter to score. The win was Edmonton's third straight.

Carolina led 4-2 late in the second after goals from Jackson Blake, Sebastian Aho, Seth Jarvis and Logan Stankoven. Stankoven's came on a pass from Nikolaj Ehlers, who reached 600 career points with the assist. The Oilers answered with McDavid at 0:26 of the third and a Leon Draisaitl power-play goal at 2:51, tying it 4-4. Juuso Välimäki put Carolina back in front with 2:40 to play, and McDavid tied it again. McDavid and Draisaitl each finished with two goals and three assists.

By expected goals, a measure of the quality of chances, the game was nearly even: Carolina 2.94, Edmonton 2.86. The Hurricanes were better through two periods, but Edmonton out-chanced them 1.44 to 0.74 in the third. In a simulation that replays every shot, Carolina wins 52% of the time and Edmonton 48%. Both goalies had rough nights. Devon Levi allowed five goals on 2.94 expected, and Bussi five on 2.86, so neither saved what the chances called for. Edmonton scored on three of five power plays, Carolina on one of two.

The Oilers have won three straight. The facts don't include Carolina's record or streak.
